conceptTag: Handle objections at a car dealership
readerTitle: "It's $2,000 cheaper across town": a Saturday at the car dealership
caseNote: 가상 사례 (자동차 대리점, 사내 데이터팀) · 모든 수치는 설명용
insight: 반론은 협상 카드가 아니라 고객이 무엇과 비교하고 있는지 알려주는 정보다. 가격을 바꾸기 전에 비교 기준부터 맞춘다.
misconception: 고객이 경쟁사 가격을 대면 맞춰 주거나 우리 제품이 더 낫다고 설득해야 한다.

sources.text: 모든 사례와 수치는 설명용 가상 예시
이 유닛의 개념 레슨 SAL-03-01 (가격 반론), SAL-03-03 (경쟁사 비교 반론)

factChecks.note: 모든 수치는 가상입니다. 계산 확인: 표면 가격 차이 $2,000 − 트림 차이(패키지) $800 − 경쟁 견적에 빠진 수수료 $600 = 실제 차이 $600.
자동차 할부·세금·수수료 규정은 나라마다 다르므로 구체적인 금융 조언이 되지 않도록 일반적인 표현만 썼습니다. 게시 전 SAL-03-01, SAL-03-03의 실제 핵심 문장과 용어가 이 레슨의 피드백 표현과 일치하는지 확인하세요.

cards.title: "It's $2,000 cheaper across town."
body: A Saturday at a car dealership. A couple has sat in the same SUV twice. Then one of them holds up a phone with a quote from another dealer.
Most salespeople hear that line as a demand. Today we'll treat it as information, using two ideas from this unit.

image.label: Couple at a showroom showing a salesperson a quote on a phone
image.brief: 밝은 자동차 전시장. 젊은 커플이 SUV 옆에서 영업사원에게 휴대폰 화면(견적서)을 보여주는 장면. 영업사원은 차분히 듣는 표정. 실제 자동차 브랜드 로고와 엠블럼은 쓰지 않음.

cards.title: What do you say first?
body: You're the salesperson. The car on your lot is listed at $34,000. Their quote says $32,000 for "the same SUV."

options.text: "Let me talk to my manager about matching it."
options.feedback: You may keep the deal, but you've agreed to a $2,000 gap before checking it's real. You also teach them that waving a quote works.

options.text: "Can I see what's included in that quote?"
options.feedback: This is the **competitor objection** at work: first make sure you're comparing the same thing. You gain facts and lose nothing.
It may be true, but it argues before you know what they care about. It can sound like you're dodging the number.

cards.title: The $2,000 gap shrank to $600.
body: The other SUV was a lower trim without the safety package. And the quote left out fees that every buyer pays. Compared fairly, the gap was **$600**, not $2,000.

breakdown.label: Missing package
breakdown.detail: Their quote is a lower trim

cards.title: "Even so, $600 is more than we planned."
body: They thank you for the honest comparison. Then the second objection arrives. This one is about price itself.

options.text: Knock $600 off to close the deal today
options.feedback: It may close the sale, but you pay $600 without knowing if the problem was $600. Maybe a smaller change would have solved it.

options.text: "More than planned compared to what? A total, or a monthly figure?"
options.feedback: This is the **price objection** idea: "too expensive" always compares to something. Find that number before you change yours.

options.text: Throw in free floor mats and a tank of fuel
options.feedback: Small gifts feel generous, but they answer a question nobody asked. If the worry is a budget line, mats don't move it.

cards.title: The real number was a monthly budget.
body: They had set a monthly limit at home. The $600 itself didn't scare them. Going over that monthly line did.

Now the salesperson had real options to offer: a longer warranty they could drop, a different color already in stock, or the trim they actually needed. They chose to drop an add-on they hadn't cared about. The price of the car itself never changed.

cards.title: Questions aren't a trick.
body: These questions work because they help the buyer see clearly. Used as a script to stall or corner people, they backfire fast.

And sometimes the fair comparison shows the other offer really is better for them. Say so. A buyer who leaves trusting you is more likely to come back for service, or send a friend, than one who felt pushed.

cards.title: Now you run an internal data team.
body: Your team builds a reporting dashboard and charges other departments for it. The marketing head says: "An outside vendor quoted half your internal charge. We're looking at them."

options.text: Ask to see the vendor's quote and what marketing needs most from reports
options.feedback: Both ideas at once: compare like for like (setup, data links, support) and learn what the price is measured against. You may find a real gap, or none.

options.text: Cut your internal charge in half to match
options.feedback: You keep the user, but your team may now be underfunded. And you never learned if price was the real issue.

options.text: Ask the finance director to require the internal tool
options.feedback: You win this round and lose goodwill. A team forced to use a tool rarely uses it well, and the objection returns next budget cycle.

cards.softwareNote: Vendor quotes for software often leave out setup, data connections and seat growth. Comparing the full first-year cost is the software version of checking the trim and fees.

cards.title: Find the comparison before you change the price.
body: Two ideas from this unit did the work today:
list: **Competitor objection (SAL-03-03):** make sure both offers are the same thing before reacting
**Price objection (SAL-03-01):** ask what "too expensive" is compared to
cards.callout: **Try it today:** recall the last time a customer said "too expensive." Write down what they were really comparing you to.
